text: Stopping to patch mid-slope (hold E on router, ~1.5s) let the boulder roll back past me; the hint then read 'From up here, walking into it (W) rolls it back (on level ground)' while I was on the slope, which is misleading: on a slope it rolls by itself. Patching on the slope seems impossible without losing ground.

Holding E on storage (57%) for 1.5s: screen showed no progress bar under the crosshair, only the static 'Hold E to patch' prompt; the patch completed after a further 3s hold. A player can't tell whether the hold is registering.

Pushing from below with the crosshair on the boulder (pt hold w 5) repeatedly slides Sisyphus around the boulder and past it instead of pushing; 'Next release' barely changes (29->28 m) and the boulder ends up 7 m behind. Pushing needs very precise centering that the over-shoulder camera does not show.
Shipped 0.1 after ~17 min wall-clock (most of it lost to the boulder sliding away and orienting). Nice moment: flag '0.1', users 10->50, 'New module: search'.
Rolling the boulder back from its uphill side on the terrace works and says 'Rolling it back to turn it'; the router's red glow (security advisory, -72%/min) came round from the top.
In first-person (V) the '0.2' terrace flag label draws on top of the module prompt text ('route0.2security advisory...'), making it hard to read.

Held R 1.5s then 4s on router: router retired (Users 100->93, Modules 8->7, 'Retired. One less thing to keep, and a few users miss it.'), but the still-held R immediately started a 'Retiring [####......]' bar on the next module under the crosshair (storage, healthy 99%). Holding R a bit too long can chain into retiring a second, healthy module; expected the hold to require a fresh press after a retire. Weight bar also did not visibly drop.

Router (security advisory, red label) sat on top of the boulder. In the over-shoulder camera the crosshair could not be pitched onto the top of the boulder from either side; I had to switch to first person (V) and look up to target it.
